extracted.intended_audience: PD(s)/PI(s), institutional grants administrators, and prospective candidates preparing NIH administrative supplement requests (diversity/re-entry/disabled investigator supplements)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an NIH administrative supplement request (e.g., diversity, re-entry, disability, investigator development) to an active parent award, including eligibility, required forms/attachments, budget, and the administrative review criteria used by NIH staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility re: existing PHS support (Kirschstein-NRSA restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students or individuals supported by an institutional Kirschstein-NRSA (or other PHS funding mechanisms) may not be transferred to supplemental support prior to completion of their appointed period of training; individuals may not be transferred to a supplement to increase the availability of funds to the parent grant for other uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals may be supported by the parent grant for short periods, at the recipient’s risk, pending Institute/Center decision on the supplement application. See Pre-Award (Pre-Agreement) Costs in the NIH Grants Policy Statement for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible candidate types and purpose of supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplements support high school, undergraduate, baccalaureate/master's, graduate (predoctoral), postdoctoral trainees, and investigators developing independent research careers to participate in ongoing projects and gain career development experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions of expectations differ by career stage (e.g., predoctoral experience intended to enhance research capability; postdoctoral experience to prepare for independent career; investigators' short- or long-term support to develop research skills). Exceptional circumstances (e.g., working with a former predoctoral mentor) must be well justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Experience Plan / Research Strategy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy section must be completed and include a summary/abstract of the funded parent award or project and a description of how the candidate's proposed research activities relate to one or more aims of the parent project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must incorporate a plan for the candidate to interact with others on the parent grant, contribute intellectually to the research, enhance research skills and knowledge, provide evidence of focus on enhancing research capability and career development, and demonstrate that the PD(s)/PI(s) is willing to provide appropriate mentorship and has developed a mentoring plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch requirements for candidate and mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a biosketch for each candidate, any mentors, and any senior/key persons directly involved in supplement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biosketches of mentors and senior/key persons should provide evidence of past mentoring experience. The candidate's personal statement should address evidence of scientific achievement or interest, any sources of current funding, and a statement outlining research objectives and career goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Eligibility Statement (institutional)
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed statement from an institutional official establishing the eligibility of the candidate for support under this program, including clearly presented information on citizenship and a description of how the appointment of this specific candidate would further the goals of this FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strength of this statement will be considered by the NIH administrative review committee along with all other material provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home Institution Approval and Sub-recipient Approval
rubrics_metrics.description: If research is to be conducted at a site other than the grantee institution, provide an appropriately signed letter from that institution; if research will be conducted at another organization, submit a signed statement from an institutional official of that organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be signed by the PD/PI, the candidate, and the appropriate institutional business official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Personnel Profile ordering and separate application per candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: List the PD/PI as the first person (regardless of role on supplement activities) and list the candidate to be supported as the second person. If requesting support for multiple individuals, submit a separate application for each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List any other Senior/Key Personnel who are being added through the supplement. Candidates must have an eRA Commons account and Commons Username entered in the Credential field; candidates should designate their specific role in the project context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH staff will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parent award must have support remaining for a reasonable period (usually two years or more). During the first budget period funds are usually provided as an administrative supplement; continued funding is contingent on parent grant funding and cannot extend beyond the current competitive segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable salary and other costs by career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary, fringe benefits, and other expense rules vary by candidate type (high school, undergraduate, baccalaureate/master's, graduate/predoctoral, postdoctoral, investigators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: high school salary must follow institutional policy and be justified if above minimum wage; undergraduate rates >$12/hr must be justified and $200/month for supplies/travel may be requested; baccalaureate/master's salary cannot exceed compensation allowed for graduate students and up to $3,000/yr for supplies/travel; graduate support must conform to institutional policies and not exceed the amount allowable for a first-year postdoc at that institution and up to $4,000/yr for supplies/travel; postdoc salary cannot exceed NRSA stipend caps and supplement may include up to $6,000/yr for supplies/travel; investigators' salary/fringe should be consistent with NIH Career Development Awards and up to $10,000/yr for supplies/travel, equipment requires prior NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial and Continued Funding rules (including renewals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continued funding for the supplement is contingent on continued funding of the parent grant and may not extend beyond the parent grant's current competitive segment and availability of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For renewals: funds for continuation of support for students must be requested as a new diversity supplement; funds for continued support for a postdoc or investigator must be requested by name in the parent grant application at renewal and may not be requested as a research supplement. Additional time for individuals with disabilities may be considered if well justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review criteria (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative supplements do not receive peer review; NIH awarding component staff will evaluate requests administratively using specified criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be assigned to the awarding component for the parent award and administratively evaluated using the criteria listed (Budget and Period of Support; Overall Impact; and applicable human subjects, inclusion, vertebrate animals, biohazards assessments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact criteria for supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH staff will consider the ability of the proposed supplement activities to increase or preserve the parent award’s overall impact within the original scope of award, including specific aspects of the candidate and plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes consideration of: qualifications of the candidate (career goals, prior training, research potential, experience); evidence of educational achievement/interest (if student); strength of description of how the appointment furthers FOA goals consistent with Notice of NIH’s Interest in Diversity; plan and timeline and relationship to parent grant; evidence the experience will expand/foster candidate’s research capabilities, knowledge, and/or skills; evidence activities will be an integral part of the project; evidence of adequate mentoring experience and success; evidence that candidate will receive research career mentoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (applicable review points)
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-exempt human subjects research, evaluate: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research that meets exemption categories, evaluate justification for exemption, human subjects involvement and characteristics, and sources of materials. Refer to Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for additional information. Only include a new/revised human subjects study record if items do not change the approved project's scope (e.g., new clinical trials cannot be added). If proposing new recruitment or use of additional existing datasets, revise Section 2.4 and create new Inclusion Enrollment Reports as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Individuals Across the Lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, evaluate proposed plans for inclusion (or exclusion) by sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and age (including children and older adults) to determine if justified by scientific goals and research strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adherence to NIH policy for including women and minorities in clinical studies must be ensured if additional human subjects involvement is planned for the supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals review points
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH staff will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to (1) description of proposed procedures including species/strains/ages/sex/number, (2) justification for animal use vs alternatives and appropriateness of species, (3) interventions to minimize discomfort/distress/pain/injury, and (4) justification for euthanasia method if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will assess chimpanzee use as they would any other application proposing vertebrate animals. Refer to the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment and whether adequate protections are proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If concerns exist, NIH staff will determine adequacy of proposed protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form and submission conformance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be prepared using current SF424 (R&R) forms in accordance with the Application Guide, and all forms must be completed for supplemental activities only (must not reflect funding/activities for the previously awarded parent award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conformance to documented requirements is required and strictly enforced. Applications out of compliance may be delayed or not accepted. Use the Apply buttons/links to access forms via ASSIST, Grants.gov Workspace, or institutional system-to-system solutions. Select 'Revision' in the Type of Application field on the R&R Cover form. Follow page limits applicable to the parent award activity code (with noted exceptions/additional requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons streamlined submission instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the eRA Commons streamlined system, identify the parent award, prepare an administrative supplement request, and answer 'Yes' to 'Is this request for a diversity or re-entry supplement?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget information should be entered for the grantee institution in the tabs for each selected budget period. Since no template exists for subaward budget info, include subaward information as a PDF attachment in the Subrecipient Budgets section showing funds requested by budget period and using same categories, and include related budget justification. Use 'Add Other Attachments' to include Research Experience Plan, Biographical Sketch, and IACUC/IRB documentation PDFs named as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: IACUC/IRB and Appendix documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, attach PDF documentation in the Other Attachments or Appendix indicating that the proposed research experience was approved by the grantee institution's IACUC or IRB; ensure adherence to NIH policy for including women and minorities if additional human subjects involvement is planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name documents IACUC Documentation.pdf and/or IRB Documentation.pdf and include them where instructed in the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier and SAM/eRA Commons/Grants.gov registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must obtain a unique entity identifier and maintain active registrations in the System for Award Management (SAM), eRA Commons, and Grants.gov (NCAGE if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Part 1, Section III.1 for information regarding requirements. Ensure the DUNS/unique entity identifier provided on the application matches the organization profile in eRA Commons and SAM to avoid submission problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Accommodations for Established Investigators with Disabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplements for established investigators who are or become disabled are limited to items that permit completion of remaining years of a currently funded research project (e.g., salary for an assistant, specialized equipment, or workplace modifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requested support must be consistent with the type of disability and nature of the approved research. Total amount must be reasonable relative to the direct costs of the parent award and the investigator's role/effort. Continuation of such accommodations must be requested in the parent grant application and may not be requested as a research supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limitations and scope restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All page limitations applicable to the parent award's activity code must be followed, except where this FOA specifies exceptions or additional requirements; only include forms/content relevant to supplemental activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must not change scope of approved project (e.g., new clinical trials cannot be added). Applicants are encouraged to submit early to allow corrections; if a submission deadline falls on weekend/holiday, deadline moves to next business day.
